title: Private deployments: VPC & on‑prem combined deployment guide (reference + day‑2 + upgrades)
author: Emily Chen
content:
Summary:
This combined reference consolidates Redwood Inference private-deployments guidance for VPC and on‑prem installations: reference architectures, packaging recommendations, day‑2 operational runbooks, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library. Intended readers: SREs, Solutions Engineers, Customer Engineering, and DevOps teams supporting private deployments.

Goals:
- Provide a single, opinionated source of truth for pre-sales and post-sales private deployment work.
- Reduce onboarding time by consolidating architectures, packaging checks, and day‑2 runbooks.
- Standardize safe upgrade and rollback procedures to minimize customer downtime.

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (engineering)
- Oncall escalation: private-deployments@redwood.com
- Executive sponsor: Miguel Torres (VP, Private Deployments)

Table of contents:
1) Supported deployment modes and assumptions
2) Reference architectures and sizing guidelines
3) On‑prem packaging and installation checklist
4) VPC network & IAM configuration (reference)
5) Day‑2 operations: monitoring, backups, and maintenance
6) Upgrade and rollback procedures (safe path)
7) Customer requirements library (pre‑sales checklist)
8) Appendix: config examples and troubleshooting notes

1) Supported deployment modes and assumptions
- Modes covered: Private VPC deployment (managed control plane, customer VPC peering/privatelink), Air‑gapped on‑prem appliance (customer hosts control plane + runtime), Hybrid (control plane hosted, runtime in customer VPC).
- Minimum supported software: Redwood Private 1.8.x and later.
- Assumptions: customer provides hosting hardware or cloud accounts, KMS/HSM integrations where required, and a routing path for telemetry (or opts out for restricted installs).

2) Reference architectures and sizing guidelines
Overview:
- Small: single-region, 2-gpu inference cluster + 3-node control plane (etcd + api services) — target for pilot and low qps (<= 10 r/s).
- Medium: multi-AZ, 8–16 GPUs across 2–4 inference nodes, 3 control plane nodes, dedicated metrics & logging cluster — target for production with 100–500 r/s.
- Large: multi-region or multi-pool setup, autoscaling inference pools, dedicated database (Postgres), and high‑throughput networking (100Gb).

Sizing table (example):
| Deployment size | Control plane CPU | Control plane RAM | Inference GPUs | Expected QPS | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Small | 4 vCPU | 16 GB | 2 x A10G | <=10 r/s | Pilot / PoC |
| Medium | 8 vCPU | 32 GB | 8 x A10G / 4 x A100 | 100–500 r/s | Prod baseline |
| Large | 16 vCPU | 64 GB | 16+ x A100/A800 | 500+ r/s | High availability + autoscale |

Component placement guidance:
- Control plane: colocate in a management subnet with restricted access; expose only admin APIs via customer-managed bastion/VPN.
- Inference nodes: placed in private subnets with high throughput networking; enable SGs to only allow traffic from control plane and authorized egress.
- Data plane: ensure storage (S3/MinIO) is colocated for low latency to inference nodes.

3) On‑prem packaging and installation checklist
Pre-install (customer & Redwood):
- Confirm hardware inventory (GPU type, CPU, RAM, disk, NICs).
- Verify OS and kernel versions (supported list: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, RHEL 8.7).
- Confirm container runtime (containerd >= 1.5) and Kubernetes version (k8s 1.25–1.27 supported).
- Confirm time synchronization (chrony/ntp) and entropy availability.

Packaging and artifact deliverables:
- release.tar.gz (installer binaries)
- helm charts (redwood-private-controlplane)
- operator manifests and CRDs (if deploy via operator)
- onprem-packaging/README with offline install steps

Installation checklist (high-level):
1. Validate prerequisites (kernel modules, drivers, GPU CUDA versions).
2. Install container runtime and CRI / configure registry mirrors.
3. Deploy control plane (apply Helm chart) to management cluster.
4. Register inference pool nodes using the packaging agent (agent config: /etc/redwood/agent.yaml).
5. Validate KV cache and model storage mounts.
6. Run smoke tests (token generation, embedding calls) against local routing.

Common packaging gotchas:
- Missing GPU drivers or mismatched CUDA/CuDNN versions -> model load failures.
- Insufficient file descriptors causing etcd instability -> increase ulimits for systemd services.

4) VPC network & IAM configuration (reference)
Network requirements (minimum):
- Private subnets for control plane and inference nodes.
- NAT gateway or restricted egress for inference nodes (for model pulls unless using mirrored registry).
- Security Groups: control-plane-api (allow: management CIDRs), inference-nodes (allow only control-plane and collector).

IAM and service accounts:
- Create least-privilege roles for S3/MinIO access, KMS decrypt, and ECR/artifact pull.
- Provide a deployment-specific service account for the agent with policies: s3:GetObject, kms:Decrypt (scoped to model bucket).

Example policy snippets (customer-managed cloud):
- S3 read-only for model artifacts.
- KMS decrypt for runtime keys.

5) Day‑2 operations: monitoring, backups, and maintenance
Monitoring & alerting (recommended):
- Metrics: per-model QPS, token/sec, average latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU utilization, OOM events.
- Logs: control-plane audit logs, agent logs, inference runtime stderr.
- Traces: sample traces for slow requests; instrument request path from API -> model runner.

SLOs and alert thresholds (example):
- Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly
- P99 inference latency (non-streaming): < 2s for configured SLO models
- GPU OOM rate: < 0.1% of model loads

Backups and retention:
- Control plane DB (Postgres/etcd) backups: daily snapshot with 14-day retention.
- Model artifacts: immutable model storage recommended; replicate to secondary bucket for disaster recovery.

Maintenance windows and procedures:
- Schedule weekly patch windows for non-critical infra.
- Use rolling restarts for control plane components with pod disruption budgets.
- Communicate expected impact to customer 48 hours in advance.

6) Upgrade and rollback procedures (safe path)
Principles:
- Always run upgrade in a non-production staging environment first.
- Preserve model artifact and KV cache snapshots prior to major upgrades.
- Provide automated health checks and rollback gates.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Confirm backups exist (control plane DB snapshot, model storage checkpoint).
- Ensure cluster autoscaler is disabled (if present) for control plane namespaces.
- Confirm least one healthy control-plane replica will remain during upgrade.

Upgrade steps (control plane):
1. Read release notes and migration steps for target version.
2. Apply Helm chart with image tag for control plane (helm upgrade --install ... --wait).
3. Run migration job: apply migrations.sh and wait for success.
4. Validate health endpoints /health and /metrics across all control-plane instances.
5. Gradually upgrade agent/agent‑based inference nodes (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
6. Run smoke tests and sample workload to validate latency and correctness.

Upgrade steps (inference nodes):
1. Drain node from routing (mark as cordoned in service registry).
2. Stop inference service and replace binary/container image.
3. Start service and wait for model cache warmup (monitor model load logs).
4. Return node to routing and validate request success rate.

Rollback procedure (on failure):
- If control-plane migration fails during DB migration, restore DB snapshot to pre-upgrade point and redeploy last-known-good control plane Helm release (helm rollback or use image tag).
- For inference nodes, revert to previous container image and reintroduce node after confirmation of model loads.
- Execute post‑mortem and tag regression with failure cause to prevent recurrence.

Emergency rollback steps (fast path):
1. Pause external traffic (redirect to fallback hosted API or alternate pool).
2. Restore control plane DB snapshot (documented restore runbook).
3. Re-deploy previous control-plane release and agents.

7) Customer requirements library (pre‑sales checklist)
Collect these items before engagement (minimum):
- Hosting environment: cloud provider (AWS/Azure/GCP) or on‑prem data center.
- Network topology diagrams and CIDRs.
- Hardware inventory (GPU model, NIC speed, rack space, power).
- Security requirements: required certifications, encryption at rest, KMS/HSM details.
- Compliance constraints (data residency, retention windows).
- Backup and DR expectations (RTO/RPO).
- Access model: will Redwood manage control plane or customer fully manages?

Sample customer readiness matrix (pass/fail checks):
| Item | Required | Customer provided? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kubernetes cluster | Yes | [yes/no] | k8s version 1.25–1.27 |
| GPUs | Yes (per sizing) | [yes/no] | list types |
| Private registry or artifact mirror | Recommended | [yes/no] | for offline installs |
| KMS access | Yes if encrypted models | [yes/no] | key policy required |

8) Appendix: config examples and troubleshooting notes
Agent config example (/etc/redwood/agent.yaml):
  server_endpoint: "https://controlplane.internal.example.com"
  agent_id: "customer01-pool-a"
  model_store: "s3://customer-models/redwood/"
  kms: "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcd-ef01"
  logging_level: "info"

Troubleshooting checklist (common issues):
- Model not found: verify model_store path, S3 policies, and agent logs for model-sync errors.
- High token latency: check GPU utilization and batching configuration; enable intelligent batching suggestions.
- Control plane slow or OOM: check DB connections, etcd compaction, and available heap memory.
